questions.question: Joseph a haemophilic male marries Sydney a female who is a carrier of haemophilia. What is the probability of disorder in the offsprings?

options.b: 1 haemophilic male, 2 carrier female and 1 normal male
options.c: 1 haemophilic male, 1 haemophilic female, 1 carrier female and 1 normal male
options.d: 2 haemophilic male, 1 carrier female and 1 normal female

questions.solution: (c) 1 haemophilic male, 1 haemophilic female, 1 carrier female and 1 normal male. XhY x XXh gives XhXh (haemophilic female), XXh (carrier female), XhY (haemophilic male), XY (normal male).

questions.question:
The given diagram is of tubectomy in females for the sterilization,
A- Identifying the correct result of the above cited procedure
B- What will happen if the fallopian tubes are ligated?

options.a: A- Menstrual cycle stops, B- No fertilization possible.
options.b: A-ovulation does not occur, B- Fertilization may take place but the zygote may develop in the tube instead of the uterus.
options.c: A-fertilization doesn't occur, B- Ovulation will take place but the zygote formation will not happen.
options.d: A-hormonal imbalance, B- Fertilization may take place & the zygote develops in the uterus

questions.solution: (c) A-fertilization doesn't occur, B- Ovulation will take place but the zygote formation will not happen.. Cutting and tying the oviducts stops the ovum meeting sperm; ovulation and the menstrual cycle continue.

questions.question: The figure shows circulation in humans with label A to D. Select the option which gives correct identification of label & functions of the part.

options.a: B- Capillary - thin walled without muscle layer & two cell layer thick.
options.b: C- Vein- thin walled & blood flows in jerks.
options.c: D- Pulmonary vein - takes oxygenated blood to heart
options.d: A- Artery- thick walled & blood flows evenly

questions.solution: (c) D- Pulmonary vein - takes oxygenated blood to heart. D marks the vessel from the lungs to the left atrium. Capillaries are one cell thick, blood in veins flows evenly, and blood in arteries flows in jerks, so the other options are wrong.
questions.figure_desc: schematic of double circulation with heart (RA, RV, LA, LV), lungs loop, and labelled vessels A (artery T.S.), B (capillary), C (vein T.S.), D (vessel from lungs)

questions.question: In the nephron of human beings, some substances in the initial filtrate such as glucose, amino acids, salts and water are selectively reabsorbed in the part X & some foreign substances like antibiotics (penicillin) is added to the urine in the part Y. Identify X & Y.
questions.solution: (a) X - PCT & Y - DCT. Selective reabsorption mainly in the proximal convoluted tubule; tubular secretion (e.g. penicillin, K+, H+) in the distal convoluted tubule.

questions.question:
In an experiment, plant and animal cells were placed in different solutions (A, B, C and D) as shown below. The outcome of placing them in these solutions is also indicated in the figure.
Plant cell placed in solution A: Cell stiffens but generally retains shape.
Plant cell placed in solution B: Cell body shrinks and pulls away from cell wall.
Animal cells placed in solution C: Cells swell and burst.
Animal cells placed in solution D: Cells shrink and shrivel.
Identify the nature of the solutions A, B, C and D.

options.a: A and C are hypotonic, B and D are hypertonic
options.b: A and C are hypertonic, B and D are hypotonic
options.c: A and D are hypotonic, B and C are hypertonic
options.d: A and D are hypertonic, B and C are hypotonic

questions.solution: (a) A and C are hypotonic, B and D are hypertonic. Cells gain water (turgid/burst) in hypotonic solutions A and C; lose water (plasmolysis/crenation) in hypertonic B and D.

questions.question: Plants lose water by guttation when:

options.b: Soil is wet and the atmosphere is humid
options.c: Soil is dry and atmosphere is dry
options.d: Soil is wet and atmosphere is dry

questions.solution: (b) Soil is wet and the atmosphere is humid. Wet soil (high root pressure) with humid air (low transpiration) forces water out through hydathodes.

questions.question: The number of water molecules required in the chemical reactions to produce one molecule of glucose during photosynthesis is ____.
questions.solution: (b) twelve. 6CO2 + 12H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2 + 6H2O.

questions.question: The reduction in stem elongation and acceleration of senescence are the two major processes that are involved in plants, and these two processes are primarily the result of:
questions.solution: (a) Ethylene. Ethylene inhibits stem elongation and promotes ripening and senescence.

questions.question: A stem is placed in water containing red dye for a few hours. A cross section of the stem is cut and observed under microscope, X shows the part that is stained red when the stem is placed in water containing red dye. Identify the tissue marked X?
questions.solution: (b) Xylem. Water with dye rises through the xylem vessels, which get stained.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The kidneys are bean shaped organ, where the right kidney slightly lower than the left kidney.
Reason (R): The adrenal glands are placed as cap on top of it.

options.a: A is true R is false
options.b: A is false R is true
options.c: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.d: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution: (d) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.. Both are true, but the right kidney is lower because of the large liver above it, not because of the adrenal glands.

questions.question: The human ancestor who was called the handy man was:
questions.solution: (b) Homo habilis. Homo habilis made and used stone tools, hence 'handy man'.

questions.question: Arpita a 32-year-old female comes to the emergency room with acute chest pain. After tests, the doctors found out that there is deadening of the heart muscles due blockage of the blood vessel which supplies blood to the heart muscles. Identify the artery P and the disease caused Q.

options.a: P - Pulmonary artery Q - Angina pectoris
options.b: P - Coronary artery Q - Angina pectoris
options.c: P - Coronary artery Q - Myocardial infarction
options.d: P - Pulmonary artery Q - Myocardial infarction

questions.solution: (c) P - Coronary artery Q - Myocardial infarction. Coronary arteries supply the heart muscle; death of heart muscle due to their blockage is myocardial infarction (heart attack).

questions.question: Vitamin required for the clotting of blood is:
questions.solution: (d) Vitamin K. Vitamin K is needed for the synthesis of prothrombin in the liver.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Insulin is secreted by the Alpha cells of the pancreas.
Reason (R): Tropic hormones regulate the activities of other endocrine glands.

options.a: A is true R is false
options.b: A is false R is true
options.c: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.d: Both A and R are false, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution: (b) A is false R is true. Insulin is secreted by the beta cells (alpha cells secrete glucagon), so A is false; R is a true statement.

questions.question: The acid rain has been a matter of concern for the Government. The release of sulphur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) into the atmosphere reacts with water vapor to form sulphuric and nitric acids, which precipitate as acid rain. Write two effects of acid rain on environment.
questions.solution: Any two: makes soil and water bodies acidic, killing fish and aquatic life; damages leaves and forests, reducing crop yield; corrodes buildings, monuments (e.g. Taj Mahal - stone leprosy) and metal structures; leaches nutrients from soil.

questions.solution: Any two: shortage of food, housing and water; unemployment and poverty; depletion of natural resources (deforestation); increased pollution; overcrowding and strain on health/education services.

b) Write the postulates of the theory depicted in the above picture.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: When you pass from a brightly lit area to a dark room you experience difficulty in seeing objects for short while. Explain.
questions.solution: In bright light the rhodopsin of rods is bleached and the pupil is constricted. In the dark, rhodopsin takes time to be resynthesised (needs vitamin A) and the pupil to dilate, so vision is poor until the eye becomes dark-adapted.

marking_points.point: Rhodopsin bleached, takes time to re-form / pupil dilates

Define the following terms:
a) Pulse
b) Photophosphorylation
questions.solution: (a) Pulse: the rhythmic expansion and recoil of an artery wall (felt at the wrist) caused by the surge of blood pumped in at each ventricular contraction. (b) Photophosphorylation: formation of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate using light energy during the light reaction of photosynthesis.

questions.question: Differentiate between nucleosome and nucleotide.
questions.solution: Nucleosome: the bead-like unit of chromatin consisting of DNA coiled around a core of histone proteins. Nucleotide: the basic unit of DNA/RNA consisting of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate group.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: State Mendel's law of Independent Assortment.
questions.solution: When two pairs of contrasting characters are considered together in a cross, the factors (alleles) of each pair segregate/assort independently of the other pair during gamete formation, giving new combinations (9:3:3:1 in F2).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A homozygous plant which is tall (T) and bearing purple (P) flowers is crossed with another homozygous plant which is dwarf (t) and bearing white (p) flowers. Answer the questions that follow:
a) Give the genotype of F1 generation.
b) Give the dihybrid phenotypic ratio of F2 generation with the help of Punnett square.
questions.solution:
(a) TTPP x ttpp -> F1 all TtPp (tall, purple).
(b) F1 gametes: TP, Tp, tP, tp. 4x4 Punnett square gives F2: 9 tall purple (T_P_) : 3 tall white (T_pp) : 3 dwarf purple (ttP_) : 1 dwarf white (ttpp). Phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Define Tropic movement.
questions.solution: A tropic movement is a directional growth movement of a plant part in response to an external stimulus, the direction of which is determined by the direction of the stimulus.

marking_points.point: Directional growth in response to external stimulus

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Differentiate between Cataract and Presbyopia (condition, correction).
questions.solution: Cataract - condition: the lens becomes opaque/cloudy; correction: surgical removal of the lens and replacement with an artificial intraocular lens (or convex spectacles). Presbyopia - condition: lens loses elasticity/ciliary muscles weaken with age so near objects cannot be focused; correction: convex lens (reading glasses) or bifocals.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor and a stress hormone. Explain.
questions.solution: Growth inhibitor: ABA inhibits growth, induces dormancy of seeds and buds and promotes abscission of leaves and fruits. Stress hormone: under water stress (drought) ABA causes closure of stomata, reducing transpiration and helping the plant survive adverse conditions.

marking_points.point: Stress hormone - closes stomata in drought

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: People urinate fewer times in summer than in winter and the urine passed is generally thicker. Explain.
questions.solution: In summer much water is lost as sweat. ADH secretion increases, so more water is reabsorbed from the kidney tubules; less, more concentrated (thicker) urine is formed. In winter there is little sweating, so more dilute urine is passed more often.

marking_points.point: More water lost as sweat in summer
More ADH -> more reabsorption -> less concentrated urine

concepts: Blood vessels in a circulation flowchart
questions.question:
Given below is a simplified pathway of the circulatory system in human beings. (Flowchart: Lungs <-> Heart via vessels 8 (heart to lungs) and 1 (lungs to heart); 2 from heart to organs; small intestine to liver via 3; liver drains via 6; kidney supplied by 4 and drained by 5; 7 returns blood to the heart.)
a) Identify and name the blood vessel that carries the highest amount of urea. Please mention the part labeled in the diagram that matches your answer.
b) Mention the significance of the part labelled 3.
c) Differentiate between the blood vessels marked 4 and 5 (with respect to the composition of the blood they carry).
questions.solution: (a) Hepatic vein - labelled 6 (urea is formed in the liver and enters blood leaving the liver). (b) 3 is the hepatic portal vein: it carries digested food (glucose, amino acids) from the intestine to the liver, where excess glucose is stored as glycogen, excess amino acids are deaminated and toxins removed before the blood enters general circulation. (c) 4 - renal artery: oxygenated blood with a high amount of urea/nitrogenous wastes; 5 - renal vein: deoxygenated blood with the least urea (filtered/purified blood).

marking_points.point: (b) Hepatic portal vein carries absorbed food to liver for regulation
(c) Renal artery - oxygenated, more urea; renal vein - deoxygenated, least urea

questions.figure_desc: flowchart of circulation linking lungs, heart, liver, small intestine and kidney with vessels numbered 1-8

b) Mitosis is called equational division.
questions.solution: (a) Physiological processes are controlled by enzymes, which work best at an optimum temperature; low temperature slows them and high temperature denatures them. (b) In mitosis the daughter cells receive the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell (2n -> 2n).

Observe the diagram given below and answer the questions that follow: (Diagram: a leafy shoot fixed in a test tube of water with a layer of oil on the water surface, the tube hung from a spring balance on a stand.)
i) Define the phenomenon that is taking place.
questions.solution: Transpiration: the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of leaves.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Observe the diagram given below and answer the questions that follow: (Diagram: a leafy shoot fixed in a test tube of water with a layer of oil on the water surface, the tube hung from a spring balance on a stand.)
ii) What is the purpose of putting oil in the test tube? Would it make any difference if the experimental set-up was kept in bright sunlight?
questions.solution: The oil layer prevents evaporation of water from the surface in the test tube, so any loss in weight is only due to transpiration by the shoot. Yes - in bright sunlight the stomata open fully and temperature rises, so transpiration increases and the loss in weight shown by the spring balance is greater.

marking_points.point: Oil prevents evaporation from water surface
Sunlight increases transpiration - more weight loss

questions.question:
Observe the diagram given below and answer the questions that follow: (Diagram: a leafy shoot fixed in a test tube of water with a layer of oil on the water surface, the tube hung from a spring balance on a stand.)
iii) Design a control for this experiment. Why is a control set up necessary?
questions.solution: Control: an identical set-up (test tube with water and an oil layer on the spring balance) but without the leafy shoot (or with a leafless shoot/leaves coated with vaseline). There is no loss in weight in the control. A control is necessary to prove that the loss in weight in the experimental set-up is due to transpiration by the leaves and not due to any other factor.

marking_points.point: Reason: to show weight loss is due to transpiration only

iv) Mention two ways in which this process is beneficial to plants.
questions.solution: Any two: creates transpiration pull for ascent of sap; helps in absorption and transport of water and minerals; cools the leaf surface; removes excess water.

questions.question: v) Draw a labelled diagram of the stomatal apparatus.
questions.solution: Draw a stoma in surface view: two bean-shaped guard cells with chloroplasts and nuclei, thick inner walls and thin outer walls, enclosing the stomatal pore, surrounded by epidermal (subsidiary) cells. Labels: guard cell, stomatal pore, chloroplast, nucleus, thick inner wall, epidermal cell.
